newsitem.title: Australia: Australian Yachting - Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting - Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
AUSSIE AMERICA's CUP CHALLENGE?
Received an intriguing invitation this week from New South Wales Premier BOB CARR, bidding me to come to Government House next Thursday May 8 for the Launch of a Sporting Challenge for the Year 2000.

The Premier's office is giving away nothing more than that but I understand the gathering is to announce a challenge for the America's Cup by a syndicate headed by yacht designer and past Cup skipper IAIN MURRAY and prominent Sydney businessman and yacht owner DENIS O'NEIL.
Also believed to be involved is O'NEIL's Palm Beach neighbour JOHN DAVID, although he may be too busy with the current war in the wholesale grocery market.

MURRAY and O'NEIL are already business partners in a multi-million dollar prestigious property development in Sydney and their plan for an America's Cup Challenge against the Kiwis in Auckland in 2000 comes at no surprise.
However, they have left their announcement close to the May 14 deadline for final challenges to be lodged with the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron.

MURRAY's design office, Iain Murray Associates, is already working on the massive design project for a new International America's Cup Class (IACC) yacht using the vast bank of computer data the office has built up in designing two previous challengers.

The syndicate is understood to already own two past Cup challengers - Spirit (1993) and the second oneAustralia which JOHN BERTRAND sailed in 1995 challenger finals after the dramatic sinking of his number one boat.

MURRAY's great record as a sailor and designer is wellknown. Lesser known is that of O'NEIL. He currently owns the magnificent ketch Cambria, restored under the direction of Ian Murray Associates, but he has also represented Australia three times at the Admiral's Cup, with Koomooloo in 1969 and 1971, and again in 1983 with Bondi Tram.
O'NEIL was also an active Olympic sailor as a young man, sailing in the Soling class at the 1976 Montreal Games with the Montreal Star class gold medallists, DAVID FORBES and JOHN ANDERSON.
PETER GILMOUR WINS IN CROATIA

PETER GILMOUR, the former America's Cup racing partner of IAIN MURRAY (they are still business partners) scored a fine match-racing victory this week, winning the ACI Cup of Croatia, sailed on the Adriatic.
GILMOUR, of course, now lives in Japan to comply with resident requirements that will make him eligible to skipper the Nippon challenge for the America's Cup in Auckland in 2000.

Sadly, the wellknown Japanese yachtsman MAKOTO NAMBA has been lost at sea after falling from his yacht during the race from Hong Kong to Osaka. NAMBA was skipper of the Japanese crew at the 1995 America's Cup when GILMOUR was the team coach.
SPONSOR FOR AUSTRALIAN YACHTING FEDERATION
Another significant move for Australian sailing will be the announcement next Tuesday that the communications company Nortel will become the major sponsor of the Australian Yachting Federation.

Again, no specific details have been released in advance, but I understand that this will be one of the largest sponsorships for Australian yachting and will give the AYF a much sounder financial basis for the development of all aspects of the sport.

The AYF has now emerged from a crisis which last July saw the then CEO and most of the staff suddenly depart from the Kirribilli office. The Federation now has a new lean and forward-looking board, including IAIN MURRAY, prominent sailmaker and international yachtsman GRANT SIMMER of North Sails, and former CYCA commodore LEIGH MINEHAN, a senior partner with Coopers Lybrand.
It also has a new president, former Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron commodore BRUCE DICKSON, and a new CEO, the internationally experienced yachting administrator and promoter PHIL JONES.
JONES, as a consultant to the International Sailing Federation, played a key role in the difficult organisation and running of the Olympic sailing regatta at Savannah, Georgia, last year.

Nortel (Northern Telecom) has been involved in yachting in Australia on and off since the Canadian based company set up operations in Australia, including two years as major sponsor of the Cruising Yacht Club's Sydney-Hobart and, more recently, as sponsor of the Women on Water (WOW) Asia Pacific Women's Regatta.
CORPORATE SAILING TO ASSIST SAILABILITY

If anyone can gain support from the corporate sector for a good cause, then it has to be yachtsman GEOFF LEE, whose ability to extract funds and services for such things as the Scout movement through to the Australia Day Regatta is legendary.

His latest project is to organise the 1997 Australian Netherlands Chamber of Commerce Corporate Regatta on the Harbour on Friday, May 16, as a fund-raiser for Sailability Australia, the organisation headed by KAY COTTEE to enable people with disabilities to enjoy the sport of sailing.

LEE, who recently sailed his fast yacht Styx to victory in the RSYS number one division season pointscore, is receiving strong support from two other sailors, JUSTUS VEENEKLAAS, chairman of Philips Electronics and chairman of ANCOC, and America's Cup winning tactician HUGH TREHARNE.
Flagship on the day will be DENIS O'NEIL's Cambria and guests aboard will include the Netherlands Ambassador to Australia, Mr R. SMIT.

Well known yachts participating in the Corporate Regatta include Brindabella, Bright Morning Star and Ragamuffin, while companies already participating include Coopers & Lybrand, Rabo Bank, Ernst & Young, AV Jennings Homes, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, Euro RSCG Partnership, HIH Winterthur, AON Risk, GE Crane, KPMG and Philips Electronics.
18-FOOTERS RACE WITH CYCA
The Cruising Yacht Club of Australia is best known for its ocean racing events including the Telstra Sydney-Hobart.
It also runs Australia's largest winter harbour series with a record 170 block entries for the Sunday pointscore which started two weeks ago.

The fleet ranges from maxis such as Foxtel Amazon down to Elliott 5.9 day-sailors, but the club will break new ground this Sunday by accepting the entry of the 18-foot skiff Bob Jane T-Marts as a competitor.

Skippered by Michael Spies, an ocean racing veteran as well as a leading skiff sailor, Bob Jane T-Marts will compete in Division D against a fleet of 20 high-performance keelboats, including RICHARD PERINI's Mumm 30, Addiction, GEOFF LEE's Styx and ROD SKELLETT's recently acquired Wild Bull, which were the top placegetters last Sunday.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
